items.stem: Name any two economists who estimated India's national income during the colonial period.
items.answer: Dadabhai Naoroji, William Digby, Findlay Shirras, V.K.R.V. Rao, R.C. Desai.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Dadabhai Naoroji, William Digby, Findlay Shirras, V.K.R.V. Rao, R.C. Desai.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: India's economy grew very slowly under British rule.
items.answer: Colonial policies served British interests, transforming India into a supplier of raw materials and a market for finished goods.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Colonial policies served British interests, transforming India into a supplier of raw materials and a market for finished goods. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem: The following statement about the low level of economic development under colonial rule is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Per capita output grew rapidly in the first half of the twentieth century."
items.answer: Per capita output grew by only about half a per cent a year.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Per capita output grew by only about half a per cent a year.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the low level of economic development under colonial rule:
I. Estimates by individual economists showed a very low growth of real output and per capita income under colonial rule.
II. British economic policies were concerned more with protecting and promoting British interests than with developing India.
III. India was an independent economy before British rule, with flourishing agriculture and handicrafts.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (b) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: I only
All of them
II only
III only

items.stem: "The estimates of India's colonial national income are inconsistent." Examine this statement with reference to the low level of economic development under colonial rule.
items.answer: The statement is valid. They were made by individual economists using different methods, as the government did not make official estimates.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (they were made by individual economists using different methods, as the government did not make official estimates.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the low level of economic development under colonial rule and answer the questions that follow.
"India was an independent economy before British rule, with flourishing agriculture and handicrafts. British economic policies were concerned more with protecting and promoting British interests than with developing India. Estimates by individual economists showed a very low growth of real output and per capita income under colonial rule."
(i) Which of these persons estimated India's national income during colonial rule? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'drain of wealth' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The estimates of India's colonial national income are inconsistent. (2)
items.answer: (i) Dadabhai Naoroji (ii) The transfer of India's wealth and surplus to Britain through home charges, salaries, pensions and the export surplus. (iii) They were made by individual economists using different methods, as the government did not make official estimates.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Dadabhai Naoroji (ii) The transfer of India's wealth and surplus to Britain through home charges, salaries, pensions and the export surplus. (iii) They were made by individual economists using different methods, as the government did not make official estimates.

items.answer: Neither I nor II

items.stem: Explain how the zamindari system affected Indian agriculture.
items.answer: Zamindars collected rent without investment; cultivators exploited; harsh revenue terms; no incentive for improvement; misery and social tension.
